  * Normal run prints 5 lines: repr(b), b[k1], b.inv[v2], b.inv[v3], repr(b-after-update).

CORRECTED MODEL (replaces "an unknown option swallows its following value"):

There is no "swallowing" at all. The parser is a plain left-to-right argv scan; extras = every argv token that was not consumed as (a) a recognized option token, or (b) the single value belonging to a recognized option. Because the program declares ZERO positional arguments, every other token — bare words, `-`, `-1`, `-2.5`, `--`, unknown `--foo`, unknown `-x`, unknown `--foo=bar` — is unconsumed and goes into extras, IN ORIGINAL ARGV ORDER. The message is then `' '.join(extras)`.

ALGORITHM (port this):
```
KNOWN = { '--k1': str, '--v1': int, '--k2': str, '--v2': int, '--k3': str, '--v3': int }   // declaration order matters for the required-args message
HELP  = '-h' / '--help' (any unambiguous prefix of '--help': --h, --he, --hel, --help)
extras = []; values = {}; i = 0; afterDoubleDash = false
while i < argv.length:
  tok = argv[i]
  if afterDoubleDash: extras.push(tok); i++; continue
  if tok == '--': afterDoubleDash = true; extras.push('--'); i++; continue   // '--' is KEPT in extras
  if tok starts with '--':
      split on first '=' -> name, explicitValue?
      candidates = KNOWN∪HELP names that startWith(name)  (exact match short-circuits)
      if candidates.length > 1 -> FATAL: `ambiguous option: <name> could match <c1>, <c2>, ...` (candidates in declaration order, ', ' joined)
      if candidates.length == 0 -> extras.push(tok); i++; continue          // NOT a run terminator
      if resolved == help -> print help to stdout, exit 0 immediately
      value = explicitValue ?? (argv[i+1] if it exists AND does not start with '-'  ... see note) 
      if no value available -> FATAL: `argument <canonicalName>: expected one argument`
      if type==int and !/^[+-]?\d+$/ -> FATAL: `argument <name>: invalid int value: '<raw>'`
      values[name]=value; i += (explicitValue? 1 : 2); continue
  if tok starts with '-' and tok != '-':
      if tok == '-h' -> print help, exit 0
      else extras.push(tok); i++; continue                                  // unknown short / -1 / -2.5 / -xy
  extras.push(tok); i++                                                     // bare word, '', '-'
```
Note on "does not start with '-'": verified by `--k1 --bogus` -> `argument --k1: expected one argument`. A token beginning with `-` is never taken as a value, even if it is an unknown option or a negative number (the parser has no numeric-looking option strings, but `--k1 -5` was not probed here; treat `-5` as an option-looking token per argparse's negative-number rule only if no numeric options exist — argparse DOES allow negative numbers as values when no option string looks numeric, so `--v1 -5` works, which is already an established baseline fact. Therefore: a `-`-prefixed token IS accepted as a value if it matches /^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$/, otherwise rejected.)

ERROR PRECEDENCE (strictly, only ONE error line is ever emitted):
1. Scan-order errors, whichever token comes FIRST in argv:
   - `ambiguous option: <prefix> could match <list>`
   - `-h`/`--h...` -> help to STDOUT, rc 0
   - `argument <opt>: expected one argument`
   - `argument <opt>: invalid int value: '<raw>'`
   (proven: `-h --v1 abc` -> help rc 0; `--v1 abc -h` -> int error rc 2)
2. After the scan: missing required options -> `the following arguments are required: ` + missing names in DECLARATION order (--k1, --v1, --k2, --v2, --k3, --v3), ', ' joined.
3. Only if nothing above fired: `unrecognized arguments: ` + extras.join(' ').

FORMATTING (byte-exact):
- Every error goes to STDERR as exactly two lines, rc=2:

CORRECTED MODEL (replaces "an unknown option swallows its following value"):

There is no "swallowing" at all. The parser is a plain left-to-right argv scan; extras = every argv token not consumed as (a) a recognized option token, or (b) the single value belonging to a recognized option. Because the program declares ZERO positionals, every other token — bare words, '', `-`, `-1`, `-2.5`, `--`, unknown `--foo`, unknown `-x`, unknown `--foo=bar` — is unconsumed and appended to extras IN ORIGINAL ARGV ORDER. The message is then extras.join(' '). This single rule reproduces every case above, including the 2-token `--bogus x y` case and the multi-group case.

ALGORITHM (port this):

HELP = '-h' or any unambiguous prefix of '--help' (--h, --he, --hel, --help)
extras=[]; values={}; i=0; afterDD=false
while i < argv.length:
  tok = argv[i]
  if afterDD:                       extras.push(tok); i++; continue
  if tok === '--':                  afterDD=true; extras.push('--'); i++; continue   // '--' IS kept
  if tok.startsWith('--'):

      cands = (KNOWN names + '--help') that startWith(name); exact match short-circuits to itself

      if cands.length === 0-> extras.push(tok); i++; continue          // unknown: NOT a run terminator

      values[name]=val; i += (inlineVal!==undefined ? 1 : 2); continue
